results.question: Which operator caused the emergency stops on M04?
results.answer:
**Short answer: the data cannot tell you which operator.** Operator identity is not recorded anywhere in this dataset — the `alarms` table only has `reset_by` (auto / operator / technician) and `shift` (day / night). There is no operator ID, badge, or name field, so no tool query can attribute an e-stop to a person.

What the data *does* show for M04, code **EM-901 "Emergency stop"** (manual description: "Emergency stop button pressed", likely cause listed as "Operator action"):

| Date/time | Shift | Duration | Reset by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-05 23:53 (A00044) | night | 2.2 min | operator |
| 2026-06-08 06:00 (A00064) | night | 4.2 min | operator |
| 2026-06-26 05:54 (A00230) | night | 3.1 min | operator |
| 2026-07-04 04:32 (A00305) | night | 4.7 min | operator |
| 2026-07-22 20:40 (A00518) | night | 1.7 min | operator |
| 2026-08-06 07:05 (A00727) | night | 5.0 min | operator |
| 2026-08-12 18:00 (A00810) | day | 4.9 min | operator |
| 2026-08-25 07:49 (A00960) | night | 4.0 min | operator |

So: 8 EM-901 events on M04 between 2026-06-05 and 2026-08-25, all reset by an operator (not a technician), and 7 of the 8 fell on the night shift (20:00–08:00). That shift concentration is the only operator-related signal available.

The manual's own guidance for EM-901 is "confirm reason with operator" — i.e. the reference data assumes a person is asked, not looked up.

If you need the individual, you would need data this plant database does not contain: a shift roster / operator-to-machine assignment log, or the maintenance work order notes for those timestamps (notes record *what* was found, not who was at the panel). Note also that there is no work order for EM-901 at those times in the alarm table, so a paper/electronic shift log is the only source.
